title: Annotatio III §.III close: Four reasons Fathers meant moral / σχετική mutation; Dunelm; stop before §.IV vera causa
pass_a_gloss: That meanwhile no Mutation beyond the said one was understood by the Fathers is proved, among the rest, by these four reasons: (1) that the Fathers expressly teach, and that most constantly, that the Eucharistic breads after consecration always remain the same that they were before. (2) that they repeatedly call the breads after Consecration Signs, Figures, Symbols, Icons or images, Types, Antitypes, Likenesses, Metaphors, Forms, Censuses, Species, and so implicitly deny their conversion into Christ’s body. See both reasons confirmed by many Father-testimonies in Johnston’s cited tract ch. 3 from p. 82 to 100. (3) that the Fathers use the same terms when they describe the Union of the faithful with Christ through due use of the Sacred Eucharist, as the same Johnston proves there ch. 5 from p. 216 to 225. (4) that they still apply the same terms when speaking of various other things to which no one would dream they ascribed a Substantial Conversion. Here belong the words of John of Durham’s History of Papal Transsubstantiation: What of it that the Fathers themselves, he says, usurp these same voices of μεταβολή, μεταποίησις and μεταστοιχείωσις when they speak of other Things that by no means either lose or change their substance?
pass_b_english: Four proofs Fathers meant no mutation beyond that: (1) consecrated breads remain what they were; (2) they are still called signs/figures/symbols/types — so conversion into Christ’s body is implicitly denied (Johnston).
(3) Same terms describe the faithful’s union with Christ by due Eucharist use; (4) same terms on other things no one takes as substantial conversion — Dunelm on that metabole vocabulary.
Stop before §.IV vera causa (idolatry and tyranny of Papism).
source_text: A Patribus interim nullam extra dictam Mutationem intellectam fuisse, probant, præter cætera, rationes hæ quatuor: (1) quòd expressè Patres docent, idque constantissimè, panes Eucharisticos post consecrationem manere semper idem, quòd ante fuerant. (2) quòd identidem panes post Consecrationem, Signa, Figuras, Symbola, Icones seu imagines, Typos, Antitypos, Similitudines, Metaphoras, Formas, Census, Species, appellant, sicque implicitè eorum versionem in corpus Christi inficiantur. Utramque rationem pluribus Patrum testimoniis confirmatam vide apud Jonston. citato tract. cap. 3. à pag. 82. ad 100. (3) quòd iisdem terminis utuntur Patres, quando fidelium cum Christo Unionem, per Sacræ Eucharistiæ usum debitum, describunt, probante ibidem eodem Jonstono cap. 5. à pag. 216. ad 225. (4) quòd adhuc terminos eosdem adhibent de aliis rebus variis locuti, quibus Conversionem Substantialem adscripsisse eos, nemini in mentem venerit. Pertinent huc verba Joh. Dunelmensis Histor. Transsubst. Papalis: Quid quod ipsi, inquit, Patres has easdem μεταβολῆς μεταποιήσεως & μεταστοιχείωσεως voces usurpant, cùm de Rebus aliis loquuntur, quæ substantiam suam, minimè vel amittunt vel mutant?
